p0.title: Cross-close open-progress retention is unachievable: the fenced source row is no longer surfaced, so the suffix can never be rederived and the plan can never be rewritten
p0.evidence: The correction answers the prior merge-removal P1 by suspending removal: "The parent design's terminal-source removal rule is suspended for an entry with progress and a null scalar until its final chunk fills the scalar. The scalar-null prune gate therefore retains the source row needed for rederivation across close" (plan:99575-99578), with "its remaining suffix remains its only path" (:99583-99584) and "Do not persist replacement operations" (:99608). The prune gate is the wrong mechanism: settlementPlanPermitsAuthenticatedPruning (packages/issuance-store/src/maintenance.ts:110-127) only gates record reclamation; what decides whether the room ever sees the source again is settlementOwnRowClass, which returns "terminal" for authorSequence <= terminalThrough (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4932) and whose rows are skipped by the outbox scan (:6945-6953). The room's only source accessor is readSettlementSources (:8687-8692), which f5b will call with the verified frontier (the comment there says the frontier is withheld only "Until the checkpoint/room owner supplies" it). Once the fence at slot m is admitted, the accepted design sets s := m-1 (design.md:165-168), and every displaced source below the fence classifies terminal (design.md:211-214). So in RED case 5's own admitted-chunk scenario (plan:99637-99642: crash after the first chunk, then close/reopen), the source row is terminal, readSettlementSources omits it, and the room cannot rederive orderedReplacementOperations because it derives them only from source.intents (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2977-3009) and throws "v3 room settlement source is unavailable" when the source is absent (:2975-2976). Intents p+1..n are then permanently lost, and because the store must refuse any plan write that drops open progress with ISSUANCE_RETRY_REQUIRED (plan:99546-99547), the room's merge (which builds entries only from currently displaced sources, index.ts:2864-2885) is refused on every attempt, so the author stalls with no fence and no recovery path. The classifier that would have to change is also outside the declared GREEN scope (plan:99662-99664).
p0.correction: Add one contract sentence and extend the scope by one owner: a source row whose durable plan entry carries replacementProgress with a null replacementSequence classifies displaced — never terminal or old-incarnation — until the final chunk fills the scalar, i.e. settlementOwnRowClass/readSettlementSources consult the durable plan for that sourceSequence; add that Node classifier to GREEN scope and add a RED vector that reopens with a supplied frontier whose terminalThrough covers the source. Replace the "prune gate therefore retains the source row" sentence, which states a mechanism the prune gate does not provide. (If abandonment is instead intended, the suspension rule and RED 5's no-skipped-intent obligation must both be deleted and the loss stated.)

p1.title: The cross-chunk logical-time floor names two lookups that both go empty after a cold reopen, and then fails closed into a halt
p1.evidence: The new rule requires that before allocating logical times for a resumed suffix the room "authenticates the recorded chunk sequences through the existing recovered/accepted vertex set and displaced-row outbox classification—no new store lookup API—and sets the next logical time strictly above the last operation logical time in the latest chunk. A missing or mismatched recorded chunk fails closed" (plan:99562-99568). Within one session the property already holds without any new machinery: commit() raises logicalTime past the last batch child of every accepted vertex (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:1913-1914). Across a cold reopen neither named source is guaranteed: logicalTime is reseeded from input.initialLogicalTime, a constant 3 at the construction site (:1811, :3408), acceptedVertices is populated only by commit() on vertices delivered in the running session (:1921), and a chunk admitted before the close classifies terminal and is skipped by the outbox scan exactly like the source (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4932, :6945-6953) so it is not a displaced row either. The specified lookup therefore finds nothing on an ordinary resume and the specified "fails closed" converts it into a permanent halt, while a room that instead proceeds allocates chunk k+1 logical times at or below chunk k's — the reordering the rule exists to prevent, undetectable because logicalTime is deliberately excluded from the binding digest (:99494-99496).
p1.correction: Pin a durable floor instead of a lookup: record the chunk's last operation logical time in the durable SettlementReplacementChunk (a third readonly numeric member) and require the resumed suffix to start strictly above the latest chunk's recorded value; or state the exact alternative durable floor (e.g. strictly above the plan's fence logical time carried through the authenticated projection base) and delete the accepted-set/outbox lookup and its fail-closed clause.

p2.title: The five-key progress planEffect does widen the public Node issue-input grammar that the scope sentence forbids
p2.evidence: The contract requires the caller-supplied additive fields sourceSequence, intentDigest, fromIntent, throughIntent and has Node "reject before issuance unless throughIntent - fromIntent equals the exact input.operations.length" (plan:99518-99525), while asserting only that this "does not add a public V3LocalIssueInput member" (:99524-99525, :99538) and that "No ... public Node issue-input change is authorized" (:99604-99606). capturedLocalIssueInput snapshots planEffect as a closed two-key record and returns malformed-input for anything else (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6244-6258), so GREEN must widen that public input grammar even though no new top-level member appears.
p2.disposition: Reword the scope sentence to authorize exactly one additive public change — a five-key replacement variant of the existing planEffect input member accepted by capturedLocalIssueInput — and keep "no new top-level V3LocalIssueInput member and no V3LocalIssueResult variant" as the actual invariant. The RED is unaffected: a five-key effect is behaviorally rejected as malformed-input today.

p2.title: Pre-sign refusal placement is unpinned relative to reserveOperation, so repeated retryable refusals can still degrade admission
p2.evidence: The contract says a well-formed effect whose entry/progress/digest/prefix differs "returns existing issuance-rejected, also before signing and without halting the plane" (plan:99532-99535), but does not say where that check sits. issueOneVertex takes an admission reservation before signing (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6354-6357) and only the catch path releases it (:6471-6472); an early return placed after :6354 leaks a reservation per refusal, and reserveOperation returning null then yields admission-rejected (:6355-6356) — the same plane degradation the post-sign P0 was corrected to avoid, reached by repetition instead.
p2.disposition: State that the pre-sign plan/digest/prefix/range validation runs before reserveOperation (or must release the reservation on every early return), and have RED 2's pre-sign-versus-post-sign handle-state vector assert that N consecutive retryable refusals leave admission capacity unchanged.

p2.title: The per-member "application-batch limits" precondition is not equivalent to what Node accepts in a batch
p2.evidence: The contract requires that "Every member must individually encode under the existing Node application-batch limits: 65,536 bytes, depth 8 and 1,024 items" (plan:99496-99498). Node applies those limits to the whole batch operation, not to a member: applicationBatchEntries encodes and decodes the outer batch under APPLICATION_BATCH_LIMITS (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:6191-6196, :236), where a member sits four levels down (batch → entries → entry → operation), the decode item budget is cumulative rather than per container (packages/canonical/src/index.ts:329 versus the per-container encode checks at :214), and applicationBatchFits gates the split loop on the assembled candidate (:6223, :6701-6706). A member that satisfies the stated per-member check can therefore never fit with any sibling; the consequence is degradation to one operation per vertex, not a wedge.
p2.disposition: Keep the per-member check but label it a necessary precondition only, and state that the binding acceptance signal is Node's own split-required/fit result, so RED 4 asserts observed split behaviour rather than a room-side limits equality.
